decision: Build src/core/grant-resolver.ts: a thin, pure-TS PDP that implements T-0015's HandleResolver port (exported via makeGrantResolver(deps)), replacing denyAllResolver at the seam without changing the port's shape. On every resolveHandle(handle, subject) it (1) tenant-gates the handle vs the subject fail-closed; (2) resolves the subject's grant set AT CALL TIME via an injected GrantSource (never a mint-time snapshot), keeping grants that are isEffective(g, now) (T-0018), whose operation matches the requested op, and whose scope contains the handle's ResourceRef (mapped to a resource-hierarchy ScopeElement) under isNarrowerOrEqual(handleScope, g.scope, ancestry); (3) fails closed ({denied:true, reason}) on no covering grant / cross-tenant / out-of-window / absent record, reason drawn only from the fixed T-0015 union no_grant|cross_tenant|not_found; (4) on success fetches the raw record via an injected RecordSource and returns {denied:false, ref, fields} where fields comes from exactly ONE pure projectFields(rawFields, visibleFieldSet), visibleFieldSet = covering grants' facets intersected with the handle's optional Facet. ResolveSubject is identity-only (no human/agent flag), so the human-form and agent-payload paths are the same call reaching the same projection -> byte-identical fields by construction, not by test. The authority math (containment, validity, meet) stays in T-0018; the resolver orchestrates. Postgres-backed ports + RLS DAO ('no direct DAO path' as a DB fact) defer to T-0053; deploy/runtime guards to T-0027/T-0028.

rejected_alternatives.option: Bake the grant set / a capability token into the handle at mint time (resolve from the handle's own grants).
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Binds rights at task-creation -> the TOCTOU hazard 6-A #6 forbids; a grant revoked between mint and resolve would still authorize. T-0015 already rejected a baked-in capability. Authority must be re-derived live from subject + current grants per call.

rejected_alternatives.option: Cache the resolved view / write it back into the variable.
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A cached view is a payload in the variable map (re-opens the T-0015 leak) and serves stale, unfiltered data after the grant narrows. Resolution is action-time, stateless per call; any future cache is keyed by subject+grant behind the gateway, never on the handle.

rejected_alternatives.option: Two filter paths (a UI/form filter and an agent/payload filter).
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Exactly the divergence the hypothesis warns turns the thesis into theater (1 caveat): two filters drift; a field visible to one but not the other is a silent leak/denial. There is ONE projectFields; both callers are the same identity-only resolveHandle call.

rejected_alternatives.option: A second authority subsystem (a record-ACL / field-visibility table consulted alongside grants).
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Two sources of truth that drift. Hypothesis 3 Q5 / 6-A #2 and T-0018 NF-1: record-rights and masked fields are DERIVED from grant rows in one table. FF-A4 forbids a parallel store; the resolver derives the field set from grants only.

rejected_alternatives.option: Resolver re-implements the lattice (its own containment/interval math).
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A second copy of the authority math drifts from T-0018 and violates proportionality (axis 5). The resolver CALLS isNarrowerOrEqual/isEffective/meet; it owns only the handle->scope mapping, the grant-filter orchestration, and the projection.

rejected_alternatives.option: Resolve fields directly from a DAO inside the resolver now (no RecordSource port).
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Couples the pure core to a record store that does not exist and pre-empts the T-0053 RLS DAO. The record read is a port (in-memory now, Postgres+RLS in T-0053) -> that is where 'no direct DAO path' becomes a DB-permission fact; keeping it a port keeps the core pure and testable today.

T-0015 froze the port as Promise<ResolvedView> (live grant/record reads are async behind a DB in T-0053). Changing to sync breaks the port contract (architect rule 7). Static-now ports return resolved promises; the signature is preserved.

fields.name: denied:false variant
fields.type: { denied: false; ref: ResourceRef; fields: Record<string, unknown> }

contracts: export interface GrantSource { getGrants(subject: ResolveSubject, nowMs: number): Promise<Grant[]>; }
export interface RecordSource { getRecord(ref: ResourceRef): Promise<Record<string, unknown> | null>; }
export interface ResolverDeps { grants: GrantSource; records: RecordSource; ancestry: AncestryOracle; now?: () => number; }
export function refToScope(ref: ResourceRef): ScopeElement; // pure handle->scope adapter (the leaf grant scope must contain)
export function projectFields(rawFields: Record<string, unknown>, visibleFieldSet: ReadonlySet<string>): Record<string, unknown>; // THE single projection; masked fields absent (not null)

export function visibleFields(coveringGrants: Grant[], handleFacet: Facet | undefined, rawFields: Record<string, unknown>): Set<string>; // union of grant facets, then intersect handle Facet; no facet => whole-resource
export function resolveFor(deps: ResolverDeps, handle: ObjectHandle, subject: ResolveSubject, op: Operation): Promise<ResolvedView>; // operation-parameterized single decision core
export function makeGrantResolver(deps: ResolverDeps): HandleResolver; // resolveHandle = resolveFor(.., 'read'); swaps in for denyAllResolver, signature unchanged

fitness_functions.rule: Action-time binding (revoke->deny): covering grant at t0, empty at t1 => resolve at t0 {denied:false}, at t1 {denied:true,'no_grant'}; out-of-window grant => no_grant; no mint-time snapshot cached.
Human==agent identical-fields: for one (grants, ref, record) a human-form and an agent-payload call-site return deep-equal {denied:false, ref, fields}; exactly one projectFields invoked by both.

Default-deny / fail-closed: no covering grant => no_grant; cross-tenant => cross_tenant (before any grant/record read); absent record => not_found; op-mismatch => no_grant; no {denied:false} without a covering grant.
fitness_functions.ci_check: vitest run src/__tests__/grant-resolver.test.ts -t "fail-closed" (AC-1, AC-2, AC-7, AC-9)

fitness_functions.rule: Scope containment + projection: ref inside granted subtree resolves, outside => no_grant; visible field set = covering-grant facets ∩ handle Facet; masked fields absent (not null) from fields.

Single chokepoint (structural): resolveHandle stays the sole handle->fields port; single-resolver.sh green; object-handle.ts unchanged; no new export maps a handle to fields with a shape diverging from ResolvedView.

No second authority subsystem / additive: grant-resolver.ts imports nothing from pg/fs/net/http/jobStore; no *_acl/field_visibility/record_rights store; decision & field set from T-0018 grant rows only; edits no existing export of object-handle.ts/grant-lattice.ts/types.ts.
fitness_functions.ci_check: ci/checks/grant-resolver-isolation.sh: grep forbidden imports + parallel-authority tokens; git diff --name-only asserts no frozen export touched (AC-11)

fitness_functions.rule: Purity / port-conformance: two invocations with deeply-equal inputs (same port data, same injected now) return deeply-equal outputs; makeGrantResolver(deps) type-checks as HandleResolver and replaces denyAllResolver at the seam with no signature change.
No-direct-DAO-path (DB-enforced): outside the gateway no Postgres role can SELECT record fields; RLS + role-permissions make the RecordSource the only read path.
fitness_functions.ci_check: live-DB probe authored in T-0053 (AC-14) — gating: activates-in-T-0053

fitness_functions.rule: Engine carries only handles & mutates only via gateway: BPMN linter rejects raw-object bindings at deploy; engine guard blocks direct object mutation at runtime, routing all reads/writes through makeGrantResolver.
fitness_functions.ci_check: deploy-linter check (T-0027) + runtime guard test (T-0028) (AC-15) — gating: activates-in-T-0027/T-0028
